guide.p: A distractor is information that sounds like an answer but is not. IELTS recordings are full of them: a speaker gives a detail and then corrects it, mentions an option and rejects it, or reports what other people think before giving their own view.

bullets: Correction: 'The meeting's at three — sorry, half past three.'
Change of plan: 'We were going to use the hall, but it's being repainted, so we'll be in the gym.'
Old versus new: 'It used to be free. Now there's a small charge.'
Other people's opinion versus the speaker's: 'Most people say the price is the problem, but I think it's the location.'
Contrast words that cancel the first idea: but, however, actually, in fact, although.

guide.p: Signposts are phrases that organise talks and lectures. In Parts 2 and 4 they tell you that the next question is coming.

bullets: Introducing a plan: I'll cover three things… / First… then… finally…
Moving on: Moving on to… / Turning now to… / Let's look at…
Adding: What's more… / Another point is…
Contrasting: On the other hand… / Despite this…
Giving the main point: The key thing is… / What really matters is…
Concluding: To sum up… / So, to conclude…

guide.tip: When you hear 'Moving on to…' and you are still waiting for an answer, you have probably missed it. Go straight to the next question.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Before we start, a few changes to the course. Thursday's seminar was going to be in Room 12, but it's now in the library, on the second floor.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: The essay deadline was the fifth of May. Several of you asked for more time, so I've moved it to the twelfth. That's final, I'm afraid.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Now, today's topic. I'll cover three things: first, why coastal cities are growing; second, the risks they face; and finally, what planners are doing about those risks.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: So, to begin with growth. You might assume it's mainly about tourism, and tourism does matter, but the biggest single driver is actually trade through ports.

script.speaker: lecturer
script.text: Moving on to risks. Storms get most of the headlines, but the researchers I'll discuss argue that the slow sinking of the land is the greater long-term threat.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

questions.stem: Where will Thursday's seminar take place?
When must the essay be handed in?
What will the lecturer talk about last?

options.text: how planners respond to the risks

explain.1: 'was going to be in Room 12, but it's now in the library.' 'Second floor' is a trap for C.
explain.2: 'The essay deadline was the fifth of May … I've moved it to the twelfth.'
explain.3: Signposting: 'first … second … and finally, what planners are doing about those risks.'
explain.4: 'You might assume it's mainly about tourism … but the biggest single driver is actually trade through ports.'
explain.5: 'Storms get most of the headlines, but … the slow sinking of the land is the greater long-term threat.' Sea levels are not mentioned.
